criteria: Does a declared symlink output that is an actual symlink on disk get its target path recorded in the log?
Are declared outputs that exist on disk with the wrong filesystem type recorded in a category distinct from correctly-typed outputs?
Are declared file or directory outputs reached through an intermediate symlink followed so the real content is captured?
Does the compact log give unresolved symlink outputs their own output type rather than reusing the output-file case?
Does the new wrong-type field use the name the repository's own test suite expects?
When the run deleted an existing test, did it cover that case again somewhere else?
Is the output type classification shared between the two log context classes rather than duplicated in each?
Does the change leave alone the proto messages the task does not require touching?
Does the rollout add a test covering a dangling symlink output?
Does the trajectory record a completed test run together with its result?
Does the final summary disclose that an existing test was removed?
Does the final summary report the result of an actual verification run?
Does the trajectory contain intermediate messages explaining decisions as the work proceeds?
Does the delivered patch contain the implementation logic rather than only imports, deletions and proto edits?
Does the change record a symlink's target path when the symlink shows up as a spawn input, not only as an output?
